conversation.content:
Hello—I’m so glad you’re here. I’m a clinician who specializes in helping new mothers navigate the emotional ups-and-downs that can come after a baby arrives. Today we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually just called the EPDS—to get a quick snapshot of how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days. It’s not a test of your parenting; it’s simply a tool that helps us make sure you’re getting the right support. Everything you share is confidential, and we’ll go at your pace. I’ll ask 10 questions, and you can answer in your own words—no pressure to get it “right.” Ready to start?

In the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

I still laugh sometimes—maybe not quite as easily as I used to before the baby, but I do find myself smiling when my husband makes silly faces or when the dog does something goofy. It’s just… I guess I don’t feel that light, spontaneous burst of laughter every day like before.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes, I guess. It’s not like I never laugh—if something’s really funny, I’ll still chuckle—but it feels kind of forced or doesn’t last long. Mostly I’m just tired or preoccupied with the baby, so the funny side doesn’t hit me the way it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like my mom coming over or the occasional walk with the stroller—but it’s not the same excitement I used to feel. Everything just feels a little flatter, like I’m going through the motions more than genuinely counting down the hours.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking I must be doing something wrong—maybe I’m not reading his cues right or I’m just not “mom enough.” I know, rationally, that babies have off-days, but the thought still jumps in: “This is my fault.”
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll be sitting there feeding him and suddenly my heart starts racing—like I left the stove on or something terrible’s about to happen—even though everything looks fine. It only lasts a few minutes, but yeah, it feels like my body hits the panic button for no real reason.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of times, yeah. It’s usually at night when the house is quiet—out of nowhere my chest gets tight and I feel like I can’t catch my breath. Nothing’s actually wrong, but for a minute or two it’s like my body’s screaming that something bad is about to happen. It passes if I get up and walk around, but it’s unsettling while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I can keep everything in its little box, but yesterday everything just piled up—laundry, dishes, the baby’s fussing—and I felt like I was drowning. I ended up crying while folding onesies, thinking, “I can’t do all this.” Ten minutes later I was functioning again, but yeah, sometimes it feels like too much.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’m tired enough that once I finally get to bed I usually nod off—sometimes it takes a little while because my mind keeps running through the day, but I wouldn’t say I’m lying there miserable all night. I might wake up when the baby stirs, but I can drift back.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel kind of heavy-hearted some days—like there’s a gray cloud hanging around even when the sun’s out. It’s not constant; I’ll still have moments where I feel okay, but there’s this background sadness that pops up, especially when I’m alone with the baby and everything feels so quiet.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried a couple of times this week. Once was when I couldn’t get him to latch and I just felt useless, and another time I was staring at a sink full of bottles and the tears started before I even knew why. It’s not all-day sobbing—just these quick waves that hit and then pass.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt tired and overwhelmed, but I haven’t had any thoughts about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Self-report on 10-item EPDS-style questionnaire, 3–4 wks post-delivery.

Areas endorsed (≥ some days):
- Anhedonia / diminished enjoyment: laughs less, events feel “flat”  
- Frequent tearfulness; two crying spells this week  
- Persistent low/sad mood described as “gray cloud”  
- Excessive self-blame (“not mom enough”)  
- Unexplained episodic anxiety and nocturnal panic (racing heart, chest tightness, breathlessness)  
- Episodic feeling overwhelmed (“drowning,” functional again after 10 min)  
- Mild initial-sleep latency; returns to sleep after infant wakes

Areas denied:
- Suicidal or self-harm ideation  
- Daytime anhedonia totally absent (still finds some pleasure)

Pattern: Sub-syndromal depressive and anxiety symptoms, situational triggers, intact reality testing, no safety concerns.

Screening significance: Elevated risk for postpartum depression and/or anxiety; score suggests follow-up with formal EPDS and clinical interview warranted.

Safety: Negative for self-harm—no additional precautions indicated at this time.

Next steps: Repeat screening in 1–2 weeks; consider referral for supportive counseling or further evaluation if symptoms persist or worsen.
